title: Practice Pack: Sound
subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 8 book your students follow
instructions: Part A checks the basics. Part B makes you think and apply.
Frequency = number of oscillations ÷ time (unit: hertz, Hz). Time period = 1 ÷ frequency.

questions.q: Which part of the body produces sound in humans?
questions.answer: The larynx (voice box): its vocal cords vibrate.

questions.q: Can sound travel through a vacuum? Give a reason.
questions.answer: No. Sound needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel, and a vacuum has none.

questions.q: What decides the loudness and the pitch of a sound?
questions.answer: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the vibration. Pitch depends on the frequency (higher frequency gives a higher pitch).

questions.q: What is the audible range of the human ear?
A pendulum oscillates 40 times in 4 seconds. Find its time period and frequency.
A mosquito vibrates its wings 500 times per second. What is the time period of the vibration?
questions.answer: Frequency = 500 Hz, so the time period = 1/500 = 0.002 s.

questions.q: Why does a woman's voice usually sound shriller than a man's?
questions.answer: Women generally have shorter vocal cords, which vibrate at a higher frequency and give a higher pitch.

questions.q: Lightning and thunder happen at the same time, but we see the flash first. Why?
questions.answer: Light travels much faster than sound, so the flash reaches us before the sound of thunder.

questions.q: What is noise pollution? Give two harmful effects and two ways to reduce it.
questions.answer: Unwanted, excessive sound in the surroundings. Effects (any two): lack of sleep, high blood pressure, anxiety, temporary or permanent hearing loss. Ways (any two): lower the volume of TVs and music; avoid unnecessary horns; plant trees along roads; keep noisy activities away from homes and schools.

questions.q: Why do we put our ear to a railway track to hear a distant train? (Do NOT try this!)
questions.answer: Sound travels faster through solids (the steel track) than through air, so the train's sound reaches us sooner through the rail.

closing: No vibration, no sound. Feel your throat when you hum!
